idiom_name: coroutine consumer of a Channel (or Flow collect)
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines collapses the endpoint into one suspending consumer: launch { for (msg in channel) svc.handle(msg) }, where the channel's suspending send and receive replace blocking queue operations and the service call is an ordinary suspend function, so no adapter or future plumbing is needed. consumeEach is the shorthand when the channel belongs to this consumer alone, while the explicit for loop is the documented form that stays safe when several coroutines fan out from the same channel (competing consumers). Flow is the alternative when the stream must be transformed rather than consumed: collect { svc.handle(it) }. A classic endpoint class is only justified when one endpoint must own acknowledgement and retry policy per message.
pitfalls: consumeEach cancels the channel when the consumer completes or fails, which kills the other consumers in a fan-out setup; use the plain for loop there.
A blocking call (JDBC, file I/O, Thread.sleep) inside the consumer blocks the dispatcher thread; wrap it in withContext(Dispatchers.IO) or use a dedicated dispatcher.
An uncaught exception in the launched consumer cancels its parent scope, and without a supervisor that tears down the whole endpoint tree.
